newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-HODDLE VOWS TO BRING ORDER TO ENGLAND SQUAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HODDLE VOWS TO BRING ORDER TO ENGLAND SQUAD.

text.p: England manager Glenn Hoddle, determined to impose order in his World Cup camp, has told his players they cannot go home at weekends or talk to reporters on the eve of matches.
The manager's tough line contrasts with the easy-going attitude adopted by his predecessor Terry Venables, and has the backing of the English Football Association.
"It's Glenn's decision," F.A. spokesman Steve Double said on Thursday. "It's because he wants to make sure the players are fully focused in the run-up to matches."

Under Venables, who guided England to the semifinals of the European championship in June, players were free to return home within days of international fixtures and speak to journalists prior to matches.
But England's tour of Asia in May, just weeks before Euro 96, ended in shambles, and led to widespread media criticism of Venables' approach.

Photographs of players clutching beer bottles in a Hong Kong nightclub were splashed across English newspapers, and the squad allegedly caused 5,000 pounds ($7,500) of damage to the plane carrying them back to London.
Hoddle, preparing his side to face Poland at Wembley next Wednesday, said he wanted a change of attitude.
"Some people may not like it, but the important thing is this is how I want it done," he said.

"There must be dedication and a certain amount of sacrifice. This is how they do it abroad, not only at international level but also with clubs. Ask any Brazilian or Italian and he'll tell you it is needed because he is representing his country with a job to do, and the job for us is to beat Poland."
But Hoddle said players would still occasionally be allowed to relax over a drink.
"It won't be all work, work, work. The lads will have the chance to have a pint or two, although it will be controlled at the team hotel.
